partner_result_applied.application: For the new diffuse-defect family every physical cross coefficient has |b|<=2/m, so the partner bound |phi_Q(t)|<=min(1,sqrt(pi/(|tb|))) gives at best min(1,sqrt(pi*m/(2|t|))), demonstrating a dimension-worsening and nonintegrable physical-edge route. Aggregate cross coefficients remain order one.

new_result.statement: There are exact target matrices A_m with nonzero spectrum {4,2,1} whose three-bank scalar core is J_3+diag(1,1,0), so two completion defects are exactly one and sigma_min(core)=2-sqrt(3), while every physical entry is <=2/m and every fixed k-by-k principal block has operator norm <=2k/m. Thus completion defects need not yield bounded-size physical pivots/minors; they can migrate into diffuse grouped rank-one squares.
new_result.positive_control: For independent standard Gaussian physical inputs, the same family has continuous output density with norm at most pi after conditioning on two grouped aggregates; this is an explicit target-valid witness, not a Gaussian assumption in the theorem.

unresolved_implication: Prove a grouped-defect recursion or energy inequality that pays aggregate bank coupling before physical coordinate selection and terminates or routes to an existing paid branch under only s_3(A)>=1.
